parsed.explanation: The objection's counterexample is valid and matches the ledger's caveat. With C={c1,c2} and F={C}∪{{c2}∪g : g∈G}, F is pairwise intersecting; transversals avoiding c2 are {c1}∪(transversal of G). Taking G={{x_1,...,x_k,y_k}: k≥1} gives infinitely many incomparable minimal finite transversals ({y_1,...,y_m,x_{m+1}}), so no finite list B_1,...,B_s exists. The induction breaks precisely where the write-up hedges: the hypothesis 'every transversal meets C' is not inherited by F_c, and F_c can have transversals missing C\{c}. The write-up derives finiteness of L only from this false lemma; no large-prime erasure (bound a_1^2) or other finiteness argument appears anywhere, so L6.2 is unestablished and L, T need not be finite.
